taxonomyNote: NatureServe names it Southern Dwarf Salamander and notes the complex has been split (E. chamberlaini, E. paludicola, E. hillisi, E. sphagnicola), narrowing E. quadridigitata.
fieldMarks: One of North America's smallest vertebrates; adults often under 2 in (5 cm) and under 1 g.
Four toes on each hind foot, where all other Eurycea have five; the one sure diagnostic.
Superficially like a tiny southern two-lined salamander.
Bronze-brown in one species of the former complex, yellow in another.
behavior: Migrates to the edges of Carolina bays to breed, in spring or fall depending on the bay.
Hides under logs or debris by day; terrestrial activity peaks with late-fall and early-winter rains (Alabama).
Females lay up to about 60 eggs in late fall to early winter and attend them; larvae metamorphose by spring or early summer.
habitat: Low swampy areas, margins of pine savanna ponds and bottomland forests; edges of Carolina bays.
range: Coastal Plain from North Carolina to Lake Okeechobee, Florida, and west to eastern Texas. Not in Canada.

lookalikes.howToTell: Five toes on each hind foot.
